title: Garment Tender Reduction: How the Garment Was Paid For — Marlowe & Finch Alterations Deposit
content:
When a Marlowe & Finch Alterations ticket names the customer's Marlowe & Finch purchase record, a garment-tender deposit reduction is taken off the deposit rate according to how that purchase was paid.

| Purchase record named on the ticket | Garment-tender reduction |
|---|---|
| The customer's purchase record, paid with a Marlowe & Finch card | 10 percentage points |
| The customer's purchase record, paid with any other tender | 5 percentage points |
| No Marlowe & Finch purchase record named | none |

**Records read.** The tender recorded on the Merchandise Purchases record the ticket names. A Marlowe & Finch card is a card of Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards — the Marlowe & Finch store card or the Marlowe & Finch Mastercard. Any other tender is, for example, another bank's credit card, a debit card, cash or a gift card.

## Decision points

| Ticket names a purchase record? | Tender on that record | Reduction |
|---|---|---|
| yes | Marlowe & Finch card | 10 percentage points |
| yes | debit card | 5 percentage points |
| yes | gift card | 5 percentage points |
| no | — | none |

## Hypothetical illustration

A gown bought with a Marlowe & Finch store card and brought in on a ticket naming that purchase takes 10 percentage points off the deposit rate; a gown bought elsewhere, with no purchase record named, takes nothing off.
